title: On-Call & Incident Response Playbook — Best Practices and Templates (2026 v2)
author: Priya Shah
body:
Overview:

This consolidated playbook captures Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response best practices: severity definitions and SLOs, the escalation matrix, standardized runbook templates, postmortem process, on-call rotation rules, quarterly game day guidance, and customer/status page communication templates. Intended audience: engineering, SRE, support, and customer success.

Goals:
- Detect and mitigate incidents rapidly with unambiguous ownership.
- Provide consistent, timely communications to customers and internal stakeholders.
- Capture learnings and follow-up with actionable corrective work.
- Continuously validate runbooks and rotations through game days and dry runs.

Scope:
Applies to production services including inference-gateway, kv-cache, batch-orchestrator, model-router, console-api, and dedicated-router. Use service-specific runbooks linked from this page.

1) Severity levels, SLOs, and alerting:

Severity definitions (triage):
- Sev 0 (SECURITY CRITICAL): Active data exfiltration, compromised keys, or regulatory breach. Page Security Oncall and SRE immediately.
- Sev 1 (P0 / major outage): Global production outage or >60% customer impact for >5 minutes. MTTA target < 3m, MTTR target < 60m.
- Sev 2 (P1 / degraded): Significant degradation affecting multiple customers (e.g., sustained error rate >5% or P50 latency >500ms for 5m). MTTA < 15m, MTTR < 4h.
- Sev 3 (P2 / partial impact): Isolated customers, background job failures, or intermittent errors. MTTA < 1 business day, MTTR < 3 business days.

Example SLOs and alert thresholds (service owners must publish exact SLOs in runbook):
- inference-gateway: p99 latency < 800ms; error rate < 1% (5m window).
- kv-cache: cache hit rate > 85% for production traffic.
- batch-orchestrator: job success rate > 99% per calendar day.

2) Pager and escalation matrix:

Primary alert path: monitoring alert -> PagerDuty policy -> automated Slack #incidents post -> Incident War Room channel.

Escalation flow (standard):
1. Alert fires to Primary on-call (ack within 5m). If unacknowledged after 5m -> escalate to Secondary.
2. If unresolved or severity increases after 10m -> page SRE Lead and Eng Manager.
3. Sev1 unresolved after 60m -> notify Head of Engineering and Customer Success for customer comms.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Primary on-call: earliest acknowledgment and immediate mitigation steps; owns initial triage.
- Secondary on-call: backup and cross-team coordination.
- SRE Lead: tactical decisions, runbook overrides, rollback authority.
- Engineering Manager: resourcing and people escalation.
- Incident Commander (IC): appointed for Sev1+; owns timeline, comms cadence, and postmortem closure.
- Customer Success / Support: customer-facing updates when instructed by IC.

3) Standard runbook template (copy into service page):

Runbook header fields: Title | Service | Owner | PagerDuty policy ID | Primary SLOs | Dashboards | Logs | Contact list

Detection & triage checklist:
1. Verify alert source: metrics alerts, log anomalies, tracing spikes.
2. Confirm scope: single region, multi-region, or customer-specific.
3. Check recent deploys/config changes and infra events.
4. Determine severity and appoint IC if Sev1.

Immediate mitigation steps (ordered, runnable commands):
1. Check pod status: kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=<service>
2. View primary dashboard: open Grafana inference-gateway-prod or equivalent.
3. Tail recent logs: loki query or bigquery SELECT on production.requests for errors.
4. If a subset of pods failing, restart: kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/<service> (only after confirming restart safety).
5. Shift traffic: trafficctl set-route <service> --weight=0 or set an alternative model-router target.
6. Roll back deploy if last deploy correlates with problem: deployctl rollback <service> --to-revision=<rev> (IC approval required).

Customer impact assessment:
- Use request logs to map customer_id and affected endpoints.
- For dedicated customers, check dedicated-router logs and customer-specific dashboards.

Post-mitigation verification:
- Confirm p95/p99 and error rate stable at baseline for 30 minutes.
- Run synthetic checks and smoke tests for critical endpoints.
- Update War Room and status page with recovery message.

Runbook safety rules:
- Do not mass-restart across regions without SRE lead approval.
- Prefer targeted mitigations over global changes when possible.
- Communicate uncertainties and escalate early.

4) Postmortem policy and template:

When required: mandatory for all Sev1 incidents and Sev2 incidents that exceed MTTR targets or cause customer impact.

Postmortem template (fields):
- Title: YYYY-MM-DD — <service> — <short title>
- Severity: Sev1|Sev2|Sev3
- Incident Commander: <name>
- Start time / End time (UTC)
- Detection timeline: chronological actions and timestamps
- Root cause: concise statement (one paragraph)
- Contributing factors: technical and process items
- Impact: customers affected, SLOs missed, business/customer impact
- Mitigation & recovery steps taken
- Corrective actions: owner, due date, verification plan
- Sign-off: SRE Lead + Eng Manager + Customer Success

Deadlines and cadence:
- Draft due: within 72 hours of incident end (IC responsible).
- Final postmortem: within 7 days with assigned action items.
- Quarterly reliability review audits overdue items and action completion.

5) On-call rotations and handovers:

Rotation model (Engineering SRE):
- Primary: weekly rotation starting Monday 00:00 UTC.
- Secondary: two-week rotation offset to overlap with Primary.
- Weekend coverage: handover on Friday evening for weekend responsibilities.

Handover checklist for outgoing on-call:
- Confirm runbook currency and last test date.
- Review open incident action items and outstanding alerts.
- Note scheduled deploys/maintenance during next rotation.
- Share Slack contact and escalation details.

On-call expectations and limits:
- Acknowledge pages within 5 minutes.
- Maximum two consecutive primary weeks unless exception approved.
- Compensation and stipend policies per People Ops.
- Team leads may reassign on-call for fatigue with 24h notice where feasible.

6) Game days and runbook validation:

Purpose: validate runbooks, strengthen handoffs, and surface hidden failure modes.

Quarterly game day process:
- Choose target service and failure mode (e.g., region failure, cache cold-start).
- Notify stakeholders and schedule blackout windows 2 weeks in advance.
- Prepare runbook dry-run plan and observation criteria.
- Execute simulation (chaos-monkey or canary traffic shift).
- Time diagnostic steps and record gaps; capture action items with owners.
- Present findings in post-game review to Eng, SRE, and CS.

Safety and abort rules:
- Ensure kill switches and circuit breakers are in place before injection.
- SRE lead owns immediate abort authority and rollback plan.

7) Status page and customer communication templates:

Status states: operational, degraded_performance, partial_outage, major_outage, maintenance.

Status page - initial post template:
- Title: Investigating: <service> — <short impact>
- Time detected: <UTC timestamp>
- Regions affected: <regions>
- Customer impact: <summary e.g., 20% of requests returning 5xx>
- Current status: Investigating
- Next update: every 15 minutes
- Incident reference: #INC-YYYYMMDD-<service>

Customer-facing update (30 minutes):
- Subject: Incident update: <service>
- Body: We are investigating an issue impacting <X> customers/regions. Engineers are actively working on mitigation. We will provide updates every <cadence>. Reference: #INC-YYYYMMDD-<service>. No immediate action required.

Recovery announcement template:
- Subject: Resolved: <service> incident — <summary>
- Body: Root cause summary, actions taken, customers impacted, and link to postmortem. Next steps and mitigation timeline if corrective work required.

Internal comms cadence for Sev1:
- 0m: Page on-call, create War Room channel, post initial message in #incidents.
- 15m: IC posts status update and notifies CS and Sales.
- 60m: Exec summary to leadership if unresolved.

8) Runbook maintenance and testing:

- Service owners must review runbooks quarterly.
- Nightly synthetic smoke tests for critical endpoints; failed checks create alerts to on-call.
- Full dry-run of runbook during quarterly game days.
- Runbook review checklist: commands, rollback steps, owner contacts, links to dashboards/logs.

9) Observability and incident tooling references:

Primary observability stack:
- Metrics: Prometheus -> Grafana (dashboards per service).
- Logs: Loki aggregated into BigQuery (production.requests).
- Tracing: Jaeger (10% sampling for production).
- Incident management: PagerDuty, Slack (#incidents, #war-room-<id>), Statuspage.

Runbook locations and quick links:
- Runbooks are stored in Confluence under /oncall-and-incident-response/<service>-runbook.
- PagerDuty policy IDs and escalation details must be in each runbook header.

10) Reliability program KPIs:

- MTTA and MTTR by severity.
- Number of Sev1/Sev2 incidents per quarter.
- Postmortem action completion rate.
- Runbook test pass rate from game days.

11) FAQs and common incident guidance:

Q: Who declares incident resolved?
A: The Incident Commander declares resolution once service metrics have stabilized for 30 minutes and no customer-impacting errors remain.

Q: When to notify customers?
A: Notify CS within 60 minutes for Sev1/Sev2 affecting customers. Publish status page update within 15 minutes of classifying the action.

12) Appendix: example timeline (realistic sample)
- 2026-02-10T14:03Z — Alert: inference-gateway p99 latency > 1200ms. PagerDuty triggered.
- 14:05Z — Primary acknowledged; War Room created in Slack.
- 14:10Z — Scoped to us-east region; identified 14:00Z deploy as correlated event.
- 14:18Z — Rolled back deploy (deployctl rollback inference-gateway --to-revision=rev-20260210-1330).
- 14:27Z — Error rate trending down; partial recovery observed.
- 14:45Z — IC declares service recovered after verification.
- 2026-02-12 — Postmortem drafted; corrective action created to add pre-deploy canary checks (owner: CI team; due: 2026-03-05).

13) Copy/paste templates (quick use)

A) Runbook header (copy):
Title: <service> — Runbook
Owner: <team>
Pager: <pagerduty-policy-id>
SLOs: <slo summary>
Dashboards: <grafana link>
Logs: <bigquery/loki link>

B) Postmortem subject (copy):
YYYY-MM-DD — <service> — <short title> — Sev<1|2|3>

C) Status page initial update (copy):
Title: Investigating: <service> — <short impact>
Time detected: <UTC>
Regions affected: <regions>
Impact: <short impact summary>
Current status: Investigating
Next update: <time cadence>

D) Customer update (30m) (copy):
Subject: Incident update: <service>
Body: We are currently investigating an issue impacting <X> customers in <regions>. Engineers are actively working on mitigation. We will provide updates every <cadence>. Reference: #INC-YYYYMMDD-<service>.

14) Governance and enforcement:

- Quarterly reliability review chaired by Head of SRE: reviews Sev1/2 incidents, outstanding action items, and runbook audit results.
- Recurring incident pattern (>=3 similar incidents in 90 days) triggers a reliability project with an assigned PM and engineering lead.

Contacts and change process:
- For playbook edits, open a PR on this Confluence page and request reviews from SRE Lead and Eng Manager.
- For security incidents, follow security-and-compliance/incident-response-security and page Security Oncall immediately.

Questions or proposed changes: contact sre-leads@redwood.example or file a change request on this page.
